items.title: Desktop: new session window reuses existing agent context (no session isolation)
items.body:
## Description

Opening a new chat/session window in Hermes Desktop does not create an independent agent session. The new window reuses the existing backend session context, continuing the previous conversation rather than starting fresh.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop — start a conversation with the agent
2. Create a new session window via the Desktop UI (click "New Chat" / new tab)
3. Type a message referencing the previous conversation
4. The agent responds with full knowledge of the previous conversation, confirming session reuse

Additionally, typing `/new` in the Desktop input field does not bypass the issue — the session context persists.

## Expected Behavior

A new session window should spawn an independent agent process with its own isolated session, so the agent has no knowledge of conversations in other windows.

## Actual Behavior

The new window is a UI-level tab only; the underlying agent session is shared/reused across windows.

## Environment

- **Hermes Desktop version**: 0.17.0
- **OS**: macOS 26.5.1 (Sequoia)
- **Install method**: `hermes setup --desktop` (bootstrap installer)
- **Model**: deepseek-v4-pro (DeepSeek provider)
- **Backend**: local, Hermes Agent at `~/.hermes/hermes-agent`

## Additional Context

The `gui.log` shows WebSocket connections establishing but no new agent session being created when opening additional windows. The `agent.log` confirms that messages from "new" windows appear in the same `session_id` as the original conversation.

## Workaround

None currently — closing and reopening the entire Desktop app may reset the session, but there is no way to have multiple independent sessions open simultaneously.

items.body:
## Bug

`hermes_state.py` line 1715 creates a UNIQUE index on `sessions.title` but only catches `sqlite3.OperationalError`. When duplicate titles exist in the database, SQLite throws `sqlite3.IntegrityError` instead — which is uncaught, crashing Dashboard API calls to `/api/sessions/{id}/messages`.

## Error

```
sqlite3.IntegrityError: UNIQUE constraint failed: sessions.title
```

```
File "hermes_cli/web_server.py", line 9984, in _open_session_db_for_profile
    return SessionDB(db_path=Path(home) / "state.db")
File "hermes_state.py", line 1063, in __init__
    _connect_and_init()
File "hermes_state.py", line 1715, in _init_schema
    cursor.execute(
        "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_title_unique "
        "ON sessions(title) WHERE title IS NOT NULL"
    )
```

## Root Cause

Commit `60b6abefd` (feat: session naming with unique titles) added the UNIQUE INDEX but only catches `OperationalError` ("index already exists"). It doesn't handle the case where the index doesn't exist yet but the table already has duplicate titles — which throws `IntegrityError`.

This can happen through:
- Session imports with non-unique titles
- Context compression creating duplicate continuation titles
- Race conditions in concurrent session creation

## Suggested Fix

```python
# Unique title index — always ensure it exists
try:
    cursor.execute(
        "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_title_unique "
        "ON sessions(title) WHERE title IS NOT NULL"
    )
except sqlite3.IntegrityError:
    # Duplicate titles exist — deduplicate by keeping the newest row
    cursor.execute(
        "DELETE FROM sessions WHERE rowid NOT IN ("
        "  SELECT MAX(rowid) FROM sessions WHERE title IS NOT NULL GROUP BY title"
        ")"
    )
    cursor.execute(
        "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_sessions_title_unique "
        "ON sessions(title) WHERE title IS NOT NULL"
    )
except sqlite3.OperationalError:
    pass  # Index already exists
```

## Environment

- Hermes: latest main
- OS: macOS 15.7.7
- Python: 3.11 (venv)
- SQLite: 3.45

items.title: [Bug]: Provider error chunk (HTTP-200 SSE carrying a 400) is misclassified as "empty stream" and retried forever

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: area/streaming
labels.description: Streaming responses: gateway delivery, provider wire

items.body:
## Summary

When an OpenAI-compatible provider returns an **error inside a streaming HTTP-200 response** — a single SSE chunk whose `choices` is `None` and whose provider-specific `error_type` / `error_message` fields carry a `400 BadRequestError` — the chat-completions streaming path treats it as an empty stream:

```
RuntimeError: Provider returned an empty stream with no finish_reason
(possible upstream error or malformed SSE response).
```

The real error (a context-length 400) is discarded, and because the request is replayed unchanged, all retries hit the identical 400 → `max_retries_exhausted` → the session dead-ends and cannot recover. The user only ever sees the misleading "empty stream" message.

## Environment

- Version: **v0.18.2** (self-built from `main`)
- Provider: `custom` / OpenAI-compatible, base_url `https://api.deepinfra.com/v1/openai`
- Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash` (context window 163840)
- Streaming enabled, tool-calling agent, long conversation (grown prompt)

## Reproduction

1. Configure DeepInfra (or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint that returns validation errors as in-stream chunks) with a large `max_tokens` (here `65536`, the effective default when `model.max_tokens` is unset).
2. Let a session grow until `input_tokens + max_tokens > context_window`. Here: `98305 input + 65536 output = 163841 > 163840` — over by one token.
3. The provider returns **HTTP 200** with a single SSE chunk containing the 400, then closes.
4. Gateway raises `EmptyStreamError`, retries 3×, exhausts, and the thread is stuck permanently (every retry re-sends the same oversized request).

## Root cause

The actual chunk the SDK yields (captured from the live gateway via a temporary `repr(chunk)` dump on the guard):

```
ChatCompletionChunk(
  id=None, choices=None, created=None, model=None, object=None,
  service_tier=None, system_fingerprint=None, usage=None,
  error_type='validation_error',
  error_message='{"error":{"message":"This model\'s maximum context length is 163840 tokens. However, you requested 65536 output tokens and your prompt contains at least 98305 input tokens, for a total of at least 163841 tokens. Please reduce the length of the input prompt or the number of requested output tokens. (parameter=input_tokens, value=98305)","type":"BadRequestError","param":"input_tokens","code":400}}'
)
```

In `agent/chat_completion_helpers.py`, the streaming loop skips any chunk with no `choices`:

```python
for chunk in stream:
    ...
    if not chunk.choices:
        # usage / model-name only chunk
        ...
        continue                       # <-- error-bearing chunk is silently dropped here
    ...
```

`error_type` / `error_message` are non-standard fields (exposed by the OpenAI SDK via `model_extra`), so they are never inspected. With that chunk dropped, the request ends with `finish_reason is None and not content_parts and not reasoning_parts and not tool_calls_acc`, and the zero-chunk guard fires:

```python
if (finish_reason is None and not content_parts
        and not reasoning_parts and not tool_calls_acc):
    raise EmptyStreamError(
        "Provider returned an empty stream with no finish_reason ...")
```

Two independent defects compound:

1. **Misclassification** — a provider 400 delivered in-band is reported as an empty/malformed stream. The user gets no actionable message.
2. **Futile retries** — a `400 BadRequestError` (context overflow) is not transient, but it is routed through the same retry budget as transient empty streams. Every retry re-sends the identical oversized payload, so the session can never recover on its own.

(Related: #56516 is another false-positive of the *same* guard — reasoning-only streams. Both point at the guard treating "no `choices` content" as "empty" without inspecting why.)

## Suggested fix

1. **Detect error-bearing chunks in the stream loop.** Before the `if not chunk.choices: continue`, check for `error_type` / `error_message` (directly and via `model_extra`) and raise a descriptive error that surfaces the provider's message, e.g. `ProviderError: <error_message>`.
2. **Do not retry non-transient provider errors.** A chunk carrying `code: 400` (client error / validation) should short-circuit the retry loop instead of consuming the empty-stream retry budget.
3. **(Defense in depth) Clamp `max_tokens` to the remaining window.** Send `max_tokens = min(configured_max_tokens, context_window - estimated_prompt_tokens - margin)` so a large static `max_tokens` can't push a growing conversation over the model's context limit in the first place. This is the actual fix for the class of bug — a static 65536 on a 163840-window model is unusable once the prompt passes ~98k.

## Workaround

Cap output explicitly in config: `model.max_tokens: 16384` (leaves ~147k input headroom on this model). Note `max_tokens` is an output *ceiling*, billed on actual output, so lowering it does not increase cost; it trades against input room within the shared context window.

items.title: /model picker slow (~5s) when custom providers have discover_models enabled (CLI)

labels.name: comp/cli
labels.description: CLI entry point, hermes_cli/, setup wizard

items.body:
## Summary

`/model` in the CLI takes ~5 seconds to open when custom providers with `discover_models: true` (the default) are configured. Every open re-fetches the full `/v1/models` catalog from each custom endpoint sequentially.

Related: #63583 — the opposite symptom (GUI/TUI picker disables probing, shows stale/0 counts). Same root cause: CLI always probes, GUI never probes, no middle ground.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Add a custom provider with a large model catalog (or any remote endpoint):
   ```yaml
   custom_providers:
     - name: ofox
       base_url: https://api.ofox.ai/v1
       api_key: sk-...
       models:
         - volcengine/doubao-seed-2.0-pro
   ```
2. Run `/model` in the CLI.
3. Observe ~2-5s delay before the picker renders.

## Profiling

```
build_models_payload: 5.41s total
├── import overhead:        ~0.5s
├── built-in providers:     ~0.03s (all cached)
├── custom:ollama:          ~0.01s (local)
├── custom:mlx:             ~0.02s (local)
└── custom:ofox:            ~2.0s  ← bottleneck (121-model catalog)
```

After `discover_models: false` on ofox: **5.41s → 0.78s** (7x improvement).

The `list_authenticated_providers()` function probes each custom provider sequentially via `fetch_api_models()` (5s timeout per endpoint). Multiple slow/offline custom endpoints stack additively. Two dead local servers = 10s of blocking timeouts.

## Root Cause

`cli.py:_handle_model_switch` calls `build_models_payload(ctx)` with default flags, including `probe_custom_providers=True`. The GUI/desktop picker explicitly passes `probe_custom_providers=False` to stay fast. The CLI doesn't.

## Suggested Fix

Match the GUI behavior: pass `probe_custom_providers=False` (or `probe_current_custom_provider=True` as middle ground) from the CLI `/model` path. Users who need fresh catalogs can still use `/model --refresh`.

This would also resolve #63583 if the GUI picker is updated to probe only the current custom provider.

items.body:
## Description

When switching models via the desktop UI model picker, the selection reverts back to the previous model. This happens consistently regardless of which provider/model is being switched to.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop, start a chat with any model
2. Try to switch to a different model via the model selector in the composer area
3. The UI briefly shows the new model but immediately reverts to the previous one

## Expected Behavior

Model should switch to the selected model and persist for the session.

## Actual Behavior

Model selection reverts to the previous model. The switch fails silently.

## Root Cause Analysis

From gateway logs (`gui.log`):
- Multiple `ws response send failed peer=... method=model.options` warnings
- The WebSocket connection drops when the desktop app requests model options
- Without model options, the switch validation fails and the UI rolls back

From `agent.log`:
- Provider is sometimes resolved as `custom` instead of the actual provider name
- This causes model listing verification to fail for custom endpoints

## Relevant Log Entries

```
WARNING tui_gateway.ws: ws response send failed peer=127.0.0.1:62743 id=5 method=model.options
WARNING tui_gateway.ws: ws response send failed peer=127.0.0.1:49163 id=5674 method=model.options
WARNING [20260626_102346_30a61c] tui_gateway.server: MoA one-shot model restore failed: could not reach custom endpoint's model listing
```

## Workaround

Use CLI to switch:
```bash
hermes config set model.default <model-name>
hermes config set model.provider <provider-name>
```
Then `/new` to start a fresh session.

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop: latest release
- OS: macOS
- Multiple providers configured (iflytek, agnes, volcengine_new, sensenova, minimax_cn, opencode-go)

## Notes

This may be related to regression #65590 ("Desktop: can't switch model/provider mid-session"), but this issue occurs even when starting a fresh session — not just mid-session. The WebSocket instability seems to be the core problem.

items.title: bug: MCP tools not available in gateway/messaging platform agents (QQ, Telegram, etc.)
items.body:
## Description

MCP tools registered via `mcp_servers` in `config.yaml` are correctly discovered and registered at startup, but are **not available to the LLM** in gateway messaging platform sessions (QQ, Telegram, Discord, etc.). The agent cannot see or call `mcp__*` tools.

This works in CLI mode because the default toolset resolution (no `enabled_toolsets` filter) picks up everything in the registry, including dynamically registered `mcp-*` toolsets. Platform agents with a hardcoded `enabled_toolsets` (e.g. `["hermes-qqbot"]`) only resolve tools from that specific toolset — MCP toolsets are never included.

## Observed behavior

QQ Bot agent log showing tool execution falls back to terminal/curl instead of MCP:

```
2026-07-16 20:46:49,101 tool skill_view completed (0.36s, 4646 chars)
2026-07-16 20:46:59,074 API call #2: ... latency=9.9s
2026-07-16 20:47:10,001 tool terminal completed (1.37s, 58 chars)  ← should be mcp__
```

After the fix, QQ agent uses MCP tools directly:

```
2026-07-16 21:01:41,256 tool mcp__ezbookkeeping__query_all_accounts completed (0.04s, 481 chars)
2026-07-16 21:01:42,310 tool mcp__ezbookkeeping__query_all_transaction_categories completed (0.03s, 1636 chars)
2026-07-16 21:01:56,406 tool mcp__ezbookkeeping__add_transaction completed (0.05s, 134 chars)
```

## Root cause

In `model_tools.py:_compute_tool_definitions()`, when `enabled_toolsets` is explicitly set (as gateway platforms do), only tools from those specific toolsets are resolved. MCP tools are dynamically registered into `mcp-{server_name}` toolsets that aren't part of any platform toolset definition.

## Fix

**File:** `hermes-agent/model_tools.py` around line 391

After the enabled_toolsets resolution block, auto-include any `mcp-*` toolsets from the registry:

```python
# Auto-include MCP toolsets so all platforms (CLI, gateway, etc.)
# can use configured MCP servers. MCP toolsets are dynamically
# registered at runtime (not in toolsets.py), so they'd otherwise
# be invisible to platforms with a hardcoded toolset list.
mcp_ts_names = [ts for ts in registry.get_registered_toolset_names()
                if ts.startswith("mcp-")]
for ts_name in mcp_ts_names:
    tools_to_include.update(resolve_toolset(ts_name))
```

This places MCP toolsets after enabled_toolsets resolution but before disabled_toolsets filtering, so users can still explicitly disable MCP toolsets if desired.

## Related

- #14986: similar issue for ACP sessions (hardcoded `enabled_toolsets`)
- #42726: Desktop skipped MCP tool discovery (different root cause, same symptom)

## Impact

Medium — affects all gateway platforms (QQ, Telegram, Discord, etc.) that don't explicitly include `mcp-*` toolsets. CLI sessions are unaffected.

items.body:
## Bug Description

The Hermes Gateway fails to establish MCP connections with stdio-based MCP servers. The error occurs during the initial MCP handshake — the gateway spawns the MCP server process, but the handshake never completes, resulting in "Connection closed" after 3 retry attempts.

## Affected Version

Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2) · upstream 9de9c25f

## Environment

- Docker container (hermes-gateway) with `network_mode: host`
- Base image: `nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest` (v2026.7.1)
- Python 3.13.5
- OS: Debian Bookworm (host)

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure any stdio-based MCP server in `config.yaml`:
```yaml
mcp_servers:
  thunderbird:
    command: /opt/data/bin/thunderbird-mcp-wrapper.sh
    args: []
    timeout: 60
    connect_timeout: 30
    enabled: true
```

2. The wrapper script executes `tb-mcp` which is a Node.js MCP server providing 12 tools.

3. Start the gateway: `hermes gateway run`

4. The gateway logs show:
```
WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'thunderbird' initial connection failed (attempt 1/3), retrying in 1s: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)
WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'thunderbird' failed initial connection after 3 attempts, parking until a reconnect is requested: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)
WARNING tools.mcp_tool: Failed to connect to MCP server 'thunderbird' (command=/opt/data/bin/thunderbird-mcp-wrapper.sh): Connection closed
```

## Additional Findings

- The exact same MCP server works perfectly when run manually from the CLI
- The MCP server process IS spawned by the gateway (confirmed via `ps aux`) but the `tools/list` handshake never completes
- Increasing `connect_timeout` from 15s to 30s had no effect — the error is not a timeout, it's a handshake protocol failure
- The error "unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)" suggests an async exception in the gateway's MCP initialization code
- This affects ALL stdio-based MCP servers that require a non-trivial startup (wrappers, shell scripts, etc.)
- The `enabled: false` flag on MCP servers is also ignored — the gateway attempts to connect to disabled MCP servers

## Expected Behavior

Gateway should complete the MCP handshake successfully, allowing stdio-based MCP servers to be used.

## Workaround

The affected MCP servers work correctly when used directly from Kimi-CLI (another MCP client) on the same machine. Only the Hermes Gateway's MCP handshake implementation is affected.

## Additional Context

- The same issue affects multiple MCP servers (thunderbird, jules)
- MCP servers using Docker-based stdio transport (via `docker exec`) are also affected
- HTTP/streamable transport MCPs are NOT affected (only stdio)

## Logs

```
2026-07-16 13:02:38,710 WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'jules' failed initial connection after 3 attempts, parking until a reconnect is requested: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)
2026-07-16 15:25:23,271 WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'thunderbird' initial connection failed (attempt 1/3), retrying in 1s: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)
2026-07-16 15:25:25,796 WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'thunderbird' failed initial connection after 3 attempts, parking until a reconnect is requested: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)
```

## Bug Description

Two stdio-based MCP servers (jules and thunderbird) fail to connect to the Hermes Gateway. Both work fine when run manually from the CLI. The gateway spawns the MCP processes but the JSON-RPC handshake never completes.

## Affected Version

Hermes Agent v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2) · upstream 9de9c25f

## Environment

- Docker container (hermes-gateway) with `network_mode: host`
- Base image: `nousresearch/hermes-agent:latest` (v2026.7.1)
- Python 3.13.5
- OS: Debian Bookworm (host)

## MCP Servers Affected

### 1. Jules MCP (Python, FastMCP)
- **Command:** `/opt/data/bin/jules-mcp-wrapper.sh`
- **Implementation:** Python FastMCP (`jules_mcp/jules_mcp.py`)
- **Status:** Runs perfectly from CLI: `uv run --with fastmcp --with jules-agent-sdk --with requests fastmcp run jules_mcp/jules_mcp.py` → 12 tools available
- **Gateway logs:**
```
WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'jules' initial connection failed (attempt 1/3), retrying in 1s: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)
WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'jules' failed initial connection after 3 attempts, parking until a reconnect is requested: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)
WARNING tools.mcp_tool: Failed to connect to MCP server 'jules' (command=/opt/data/bin/jules-mcp-wrapper.sh): Connection closed
```

### 2. Thunderbird MCP (Node.js, tb-mcp)
- **Command:** `/opt/data/bin/thunderbird-mcp-wrapper.sh`
- **Implementation:** Node.js (`thunderbird-cli-mcp`)
- **Status:** Runs perfectly from CLI: `tb-mcp` → "thunderbird-cli MCP server running on stdio (12 tools)"
- **Gateway logs:**
```
WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'thunderbird' initial connection failed (attempt 1/3), retrying in 1s: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)
WARNING tools.mcp_tool: MCP server 'thunderbird' failed initial connection after 3 attempts, parking until a reconnect is requested: unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)
WARNING tools.mcp_tool: Failed to connect to MCP server 'thunderbird' (command=/opt/data/bin/thunderbird-mcp-wrapper.sh): Connection closed
```

## Analysis

### What works:
- Both MCP servers start successfully when run directly from the container shell
- Both report their tools correctly (12 tools each)
- The MCP processes are visible in `ps aux` after the gateway spawns them
- The wrapper scripts (`thunderbird-mcp-wrapper.sh`, `jules-mcp-wrapper.sh`) are executable and contain correct paths

### What fails:
- The gateway's MCP initialization handshake (`tools/list` via JSON-RPC over stdio) never completes
- The error "unhandled errors in a TaskGroup (1 sub-exception)" suggests an asynchronous exception in the gateway's MCP connection code
- Increasing `connect_timeout` from 15s to 30s had no effect — the error is not a timeout
- The `enabled: false` flag on MCP servers is also ignored — the gateway attempts to connect even to disabled MCP servers

### Comparison:
- Both MCP servers work correctly with other MCP clients (Kimi-CLI, Claude Code)
- HTTP/streamable transport MCPs in the same Hermes config work fine (e.g., brave-search, filesystem, github)
- Only stdio-transport MCP servers with wrapper scripts are affected

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure in `config.yaml`:
```yaml
mcp_servers:
  jules:
    command: /opt/data/bin/jules-mcp-wrapper.sh
    args: []
    enabled: true
  thunderbird:
    command: /opt/data/bin/thunderbird-mcp-wrapper.sh
    args: []
    enabled: true
```

2. Start gateway: `hermes gateway run`

3. Observe repeated connection failures every ~3 seconds

## Expected Behavior

Gateway should successfully complete the MCP handshake with stdio-based MCP servers, allowing them to register their tools.

## Additional Context

- Issue #65673 (same root cause — gateway MCP handshake)

Summary
The desktop app's backend (HERMES_DESKTOP=1) starts its own cron ticker (hermes_cli/web_server.py → _start_desktop_cron_ticker). That process never runs the config.yaml → TERMINAL_* environment bridge, which only exists in cli.py (load_cli_config, module-level) and gateway/run.py (module-level). Since tools/terminal_tool.py:_get_env_config() resolves the backend exclusively via os.getenv("TERMINAL_ENV", "local"), every cron job the desktop ticker wins is executed with a local environment — even when terminal.backend: docker is configured.

Impact
Reliability: File tools targeting container paths fail with File not found: /workspace/... / write_file: .hermes-tmp.XXX: No such file or directory. Because the desktop ticker and a running gateway race for cron/.tick.lock per tick, failures look intermittent (whoever wins determines the backend), which makes this very hard to diagnose. We chased phantom Docker/virtiofs issues for days.

Sandbox bypass (security-relevant): A cron agent that is supposed to be jailed in a --network=none Docker sandbox silently gets unsandboxed host execution with network access for its terminal/file/code tools whenever the desktop ticker wins the race.

Reproduction (v0.18.0, macOS/arm64, Docker via Colima)
Configure terminal.backend: docker in ~/.hermes/config.yaml (edit the file directly; do not use hermes config set, which also mirrors the value into .env and masks the bug). Add a docker_volumes mount, e.g. ~/Documents/Hermes:/workspace/main:rw.

Create a recurring cron job whose prompt reads/writes a file under /workspace/main/....

Run the desktop app (its backend must be up) — with or without a gateway.

Observe scheduled runs: whenever the desktop backend wins the tick, the run logs tools.file_tools: Creating new local environment for task default and file ops fail with the errors above. Runs won by a gateway log Creating new docker environment + Docker volume_args: [...] and succeed.

Expected
The desktop ticker should execute cron jobs with the same terminal backend resolution as the gateway/CLI — terminal.backend from config.yaml should be honored in every process that can execute agent tool calls.

Suggested fix
Run the same config→env bridge during serve/web_server startup (or make _get_env_config() fall back to config.yaml instead of defaulting to "local" when TERMINAL_ENV is unset). Alternatively, refuse to run cron jobs in a process whose terminal config is unresolved.

Workaround (confirmed)
Mirror the terminal.* settings as TERMINAL_* variables into ~/.hermes/.env (loaded by every process via load_hermes_dotenv), e.g. TERMINAL_ENV=docker, TERMINAL_DOCKER_VOLUMES=[...], TERMINAL_DOCKER_EXTRA_ARGS=["--network=none",...] — this is what hermes config set terminal.* would have written anyway.

items.body:
# Bug: Saving an OpenRouter API key never clears `auth.json` `active_provider`, so the app keeps using Nous Portal

## Summary
When a user saves an OpenRouter API key (a non-OAuth / API-key provider) in the desktop app's settings, Hermes:
1. writes the key to `.env` correctly, and
2. saves `model.provider: openrouter` to `config.yaml` correctly,

— but **never clears `auth.json`'s `active_provider`**, which stays pinned to `"nous"` (the OAuth Nous Portal the user originally logged into). At runtime, provider resolution reads `auth.json.active_provider` **first** and only falls back to `config.yaml.model.provider` when `active_provider` is `null`. Because it stays `"nous"`, every session launches on `provider=nous` / `https://inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1`, and:
- the OpenRouter model picker appears broken (selections look like no-ops), and
- a **resumed** chat session is permanently locked to `nous` (provider is read at session creation; prompt-caching intentionally prevents hot-swapping it mid-session).

The user's OpenRouter key is valid and OpenRouter is fully reachable — the app simply never routes to it. This is **not** a backend crash on OpenRouter and **not** a stale-process issue.

## Environment
- **App:** Hermes Agent desktop (native Electron app)
- **Version:** v0.18.2 (2026.7.7.2), upstream `53adb3fd`, install method: `git`
- **OS:** Windows 11, hostname `Worldsmith`
- **Python:** 3.11.15 — OpenAI SDK 2.24.0
- **HERMES_HOME:** `C:\Users\Worldsmith\AppData\Local\hermes`

## Steps to reproduce
1. Fresh-ish install where the user completed the Nous Portal OAuth device-code login, so `auth.json` has `"active_provider": "nous"` and a nous credential in the pool.
2. Open the desktop app → **Settings → enter an OpenRouter API key** (`sk-or-...`).
3. (Key saved to `.env`; `config.yaml` gains `model.provider: openrouter`.)
4. Pick an OpenRouter model in the picker, or restart the app, or reboot.

## Expected behavior
- OpenRouter becomes the active provider.
- New sessions launch against `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1` using the OpenRouter key.
- The picker lists and lets the user select OpenRouter's catalog (342+ models).

## Actual behavior
- `config.yaml` says `model.provider: openrouter` (correct).
- `auth.json` still says `active_provider: "nous"` (never cleared).
- Every new session logs `provider=nous base_url=https://inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1`.
- A resumed session stays on `nous` permanently (1059+ API calls observed on nous for one session).

## Root cause (code-verified)
Provider resolution priority is `auth.json.active_provider` **first**, then `config.yaml.model.provider` as fallback.

- `hermes_cli/auth.py::get_active_provider()` (line ~1480) returns `auth_store.get("active_provider")` first; downstream resolution consults it before config.
- `auth.json` retains `"active_provider": "nous"` after the OpenRouter key is added. Nothing in the key-save / settings flow calls `deactivate_provider()` — the function explicitly built for exactly this case: *"user switches to a non-OAuth provider (OpenRouter, custom) so auto-resolution doesn't keep picking the OAuth provider"* (`hermes_cli/auth.py:1604`).
- `mark_provider_active_if_unset(provider)` (auth.py:1271) only re-pins `active_provider` **if it is currently unset** (`if not auth_store.get("active_provider")`). With `active_provider="nous"` already set, it correctly stays `nous` — so the stale OAuth provider wins until something explicitly clears it.

Verified by executing the resolution path against live state:
```python
from hermes_cli.auth import get_active_provider
from hermes_cli import config as cfg
mp = cfg.load_config().get("model", {})
active = get_active_provider()            # "nous" (stale)
resolved = active if active else mp.get("provider")   # -> "nous", ignores "openrouter"
```
After `hermes logout --provider nous` (which sets `active_provider=null` via `clear_provider_auth`):
```python
active = get_active_provider()            # None
resolved = active if active else mp.get("provider")   # -> "openrouter"
```
A real OpenRouter API call through the resolved client returns a valid completion — **no crash, no 400, no auth error**.

## Fix / workaround (verified)
The settings key-save / provider-setup flow should call `deactivate_provider()` (or otherwise clear `active_provider`) whenever the chosen provider is a non-OAuth / API-key provider (OpenRouter, custom, etc.). This function already exists for this purpose — it just isn't wired into the save path.

Manual equivalent that fixed it on the user's machine:
```bash
hermes logout --provider nous
# -> "Logged out of Nous Portal." (clears active_provider to null; preserves OpenRouter key)
hermes config set model.provider openrouter   # already correct
```
After that, start a **new** chat (a resumed session stays on its original provider by design). New sessions resolve to OpenRouter.

## Secondary observations
- **Resumed sessions can't hot-swap providers.** Provider is read at session creation; prompt-caching prevents mid-session provider swaps. The picker gives no warning that switching providers requires a new session, so it *looks* like the selection did nothing. A warning ("switching providers starts a new session") would prevent this confusion.
- **Transient crash during provider flips (separate from the root cause).** While `active_provider` flip-flopped between `nous` and `null` (e.g. during logout/config churn), `desktop.log` showed `Hermes backend exited (1)` followed by a backend restart. This was a watchdog restart race, not an OpenRouter-specific crash — once `active_provider` is stably `null`, the backend is healthy (`HERMES_BACKEND_READY`, no exit-1). Worth noting in case there's a separate restart-loop bug when `active_provider` transitions.
- **`openrouter` has no static `_PROVIDER_MODELS` entry** in `hermes_cli/models.py`; its picker listing depends 100% on the live `/api/v1/models` fetch. If that fetch fails, OpenRouter shows zero models with no static fallback (every other provider has one).

## Suggested fixes
1. **Primary:** In the settings key-save / provider-setup flow, call `deactivate_provider()` when the chosen provider is non-OAuth / API-key (OpenRouter, custom, etc.). Already exists for this exact case — just not wired into the save path.
2. Make `model.provider` in `config.yaml` authoritative when explicitly set: if `config.yaml.model.provider` names a provider with valid credentials, it should win over a stale `auth.json.active_provider`, or they should be reconciled on startup.
3. When `active_provider` (OAuth) and `model.provider` (config) disagree, surface a one-line nudge in the UI rather than silently using the OAuth one.
4. When the user picks a model on a *different* provider than the current session's provider, warn that this applies to new sessions (or offer to start one) — don't let the selection silently no-op on a resumed session.
5. Give `openrouter` a static fallback in `_PROVIDER_MODELS` so the picker degrades gracefully if the live catalog fetch fails.
6. Validate the key at save time (`GET /api/v1/models` with the bearer token) and show a success/failure toast.

## Attachments / evidence
- `$HERMES_HOME/.env`: `OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-...` present and valid (verified: real `chat.completions` call via the resolved OpenRouter client returned a valid completion).
- `$HERMES_HOME/config.yaml`: `model.provider: openrouter` (correct).
- `$HERMES_HOME/auth.json`: `active_provider: "nous"` before fix; `null` after `hermes logout --provider nous`.
- `agent.log`: resumed session `20260716_085519_516ce0` made 1059 API calls on `provider=nous` — never switched.
- `get_active_provider()` executed directly returned `"nous"` and overrode `config.yaml`; after logout returned `None` and resolution fell through to `openrouter`.
- `desktop.log`: `Hermes backend exited (1)` observed **only** during `active_provider` flip-flop churn; stable once `active_provider=null`.

items.body:
## Summary

The Hermes desktop app's sidebar displays Telegram (and other messaging platform) sessions from **all profiles** regardless of which profile is currently active. When switching to a profile that has no Telegram gateway configured (e.g., a local-only profile), sessions from other profiles' Telegram conversations still appear in the sidebar's "TELEGRAM" section.

## Expected behavior

When a specific profile is selected in the profile switcher, the messaging/Telegram section of the sidebar should only show sessions belonging to that profile — consistent with how local (desktop/cli) sessions are already filtered by profile scope.

## Actual behavior

Local sessions are correctly filtered by profile (line 369 of `apps/desktop/src/app/chat/sidebar/index.tsx`):

```ts
const scopedSessions = useMemo(
  () => (showAllProfiles ? sessions : sessions.filter(s => normalizeProfileKey(s.profile) === profileScope)),
  [sessions, showAllProfiles, profileScope]
);
```

However, messaging sessions are fetched with a hardcoded `profile: 'all'` parameter in `apps/desktop/src/app/session/hooks/use-session-list-actions.ts`:

```ts
const refreshMessagingSessions = useCallback(async () => {
  try {
    const result = await listAllProfileSessions(MESSAGING_SECTION_LIMIT, 1, 'exclude', 'recent', 'all', {
      excludeSources: MESSAGING_EXCLUDED_SOURCES
    })
    // ...
  }
}, [])
```

The `'all'` value (5th argument to `listAllProfileSessions`) means messaging sessions are fetched across every profile, and no filtering by `profileScope` is applied afterward. This causes Telegram sessions from the default profile to appear in the sidebar even when a different profile (e.g., a local-only profile with no Telegram gateway) is active.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Create a local-only profile (e.g., `gori`) with no Telegram gateway
2. Have the default profile running with a Telegram gateway connected and some Telegram conversation history
3. Open the Hermes desktop app
4. Switch to the `gori` profile in the sidebar profile switcher
5. Observe: the "TELEGRAM" section still shows sessions from the default profile's Telegram conversations

## Environment

- **Hermes version**: 0.18.2
- **OS**: macOS 26.5.2
- **Profiles**: `default` (with Telegram gateway), `gori` (local-only, no gateway)

## Suggested fix

Pass the active `profileScope` to `listAllProfileSessions` in `refreshMessagingSessions` and `loadMoreMessagingForPlatform` instead of the hardcoded `'all'`, so messaging sessions are filtered by the selected profile:

```ts
// In refreshMessagingSessions:
const profileParam = profileScope === ALL_PROFILES ? 'all' : profileScope
const result = await listAllProfileSessions(MESSAGING_SECTION_LIMIT, 1, 'exclude', 'recent', profileParam, {
  excludeSources: MESSAGING_EXCLUDED_SOURCES
})
```

This mirrors the pattern already used for local sessions and the `refreshSessions` callback which already passes `sessionProfile`:

```ts
const sessionProfile = profileScope === ALL_PROFILES ? 'all' : profileScope
const result = await listAllProfileSessions(limit, 1, 'exclude', 'recent', sessionProfile, {
  excludeSources: SIDEBAR_EXCLUDED_SOURCES
})
```

## Impact

Privacy concern: a user switching to a local/private profile can see conversation titles (and resume them) from other profiles' Telegram sessions in the sidebar. For users who explicitly set up isolated local profiles (e.g., for privacy or offline use), this is unexpected and potentially concerning.

items.body:
three locations in the codebase pass untrusted or user-influenced strings to `subprocess.run(..., shell=True)`. `shell=True` causes the command string to be parsed by the shell, enabling metacharacter injection if any interpolated value is attacker-controlled.

---

**Site 1 — `hermes_cli/mcp_catalog.py:367`**

**Context:** `_run_bootstrap_commands()` runs commands from an MCP catalog entry's `bootstrap` field. These entries are loaded from user-managed JSON (`mcp-catalog.json`).

**Current code:**
python
for cmd in commands:
    proc = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=str(cwd), shell=True)
**Risk:** `cmd` is a raw string from the catalog JSON. A malicious catalog entry can inject shell metacharacters.

**Suggested fix:** If `cmd` is always a simple single command, use `subprocess.run(shlex.split(cmd), cwd=str(cwd))`. If `&&` / `||` chaining is required, parse the command safely or require a list-of-strings format in the catalog schema.

---

**Site 2 — `hermes_cli/web_server.py:4646`**

**Context:** Plugin install handler runs `npm install` / `pip install` strings from third-party plugin manifests.

**Current code:**
python
install = _run_setup_command(
    install_cmd,
    display=install_cmd,
    shell=True,
    timeout=300,
)
**Risk:** `install_cmd` comes from a plugin's `plugin.yaml` or manifest. A malicious plugin can inject via shell metacharacters.

**Suggested fix:** For `npm install` and `pip install` specifically, split into list form (`["npm", "install"]` or `["pip", "install", "-r", "requirements.txt"]`) instead of shell strings. The `_run_setup_command()` helper should accept a list and pass it without `shell=True`.

---

**Site 3 — `tools/transcription_tools.py:1237`**

**Context:** Local STT command runs a user-provided template string.

**Current code:**
python (1/2)
:heart:
Click to react
:metal:
Click to react
:100:
Click to react
Add Reaction
Reply
Forward
More

use_shell = bool(os.getenv(LOCAL_STT_COMMAND_ENV, "").strip())
if use_shell:
    subprocess.run(command, shell=True, ...)
**Risk:** `command` is built from a template string supplied via `LOCAL_STT_COMMAND_ENV`. While individual interpolated values are `shlex.quote()`-wrapped before formatting, the template itself is executed via `shell=True`. A malicious template (e.g., `"; rm -rf /; #`) executes arbitrary code.

**Suggested fix:** Always use `shlex.split(command)` and pass as a list to `subprocess.run()` without `shell=True`. If the template genuinely needs shell features, document the requirement and validate the template against an allowlist of safe patterns.

---

**Severity:** Medium-to-High — all three require the attacker to control a catalog entry, plugin manifest, or env var respectively, but the blast radius is arbitrary code execution in the Hermes process context.

+```markdown
+## Summary
+
+In the Hermes Desktop app, sessions list in the sidebar but you cannot click into the workspace the session belongs to. Wanting the equivalent of **Cursor 3.0's Workspace → sessions nested tree**: click a session, sidebar/workdir switches to that session's recorded workspace.
+
+This is the GUI half of the work already tracked in **#48190** (Session ↔ Workspace binding). §1–§3 of that issue (record cwd/repo/branch, list with a workspace column, restore cwd on `-r/--continue`) were implemented in PR #48591 — thank you — but §4 "Desktop GUI sidebar grouping" was explicitly left as a stretch goal there. This issue picks up that stretch and turns it into a concrete UI request.

+After the CLI side lands, a session row in the SQLite store already carries:
+- `cwd`
+- `git_remote` (normalized, secrets stripped)
+- `git_branch`
+- `workspace` (stable human name, defaults to repo basename)
+
+The Desktop sidebar already shows sessions; what it does **not** do is link those sessions to a workspace surface you can switch into from inside the GUI. Today the only way to "get back to" the workspace a session was created in is to manually `cd` in the embedded terminal — which defeats the whole point of the binding.
+
+Use case: I run ~8 active repos in parallel. After a context switch (close laptop, reopen next day), I want to:
+1. Pick a session from yesterday's `repoA` work.
+2. Have the sidebar land on the `repoA` workspace, the embedded terminal `cd` into the right repo/branch, and any follow-up tool calls (read_file / terminal) automatically scoped to that workspace.
+
+That one-key "session → workspace" jump is the daily-driver interaction I'm missing.
+
+## Proposed behavior
+
+### A. Sidebar click-to-jump
+- Hovering a session in the sidebar shows its recorded workspace as a chip (e.g. `repoA · main`).
+- Clicking that chip (or a dedicated icon on the session row) calls `project_switch` (or equivalent) for that workspace — same primitive the `project_switch` tool already exposes to the agent.
+- The embedded terminal's cwd follows.
+
+### B. Visual grouping (optional but nice)
+- Add a "Group by workspace" toggle to the sidebar filter.
+- Renders as `Workspace → [sessions]` (the Cursor 3.0 layout #48190 §4 describes).
+
+### C. "Open workspace" affordance
+- Even when grouping is off, give each session row a `↗` action that opens the workspace in a new desktop Project pane, in case the user wants to keep the current workspace and just peek at the other one side-by-side.
+

+- No per-turn token impact — this is purely read-side UI over the existing session store.
+
+## Acceptance criteria
+
+- [ ] Hovering a session row shows its workspace chip.
+- [ ] Clicking the chip switches the active Desktop workspace (or opens a new one) and `cd`'s the embedded terminal into the recorded cwd.
+- [ ] Missing-cwd sessions are handled gracefully (warning + relocation prompt).
+- [ ] Sessions with `workspace=null` still display a chip based on `cwd`.
+- [ ] Existing CLI behavior from #48190 / #48591 is unaffected.
+
+## Related
+
+- #48190 — original feature request (CLI side, partially implemented in #48591)
+- #56701 — shared workspace concept across profiles (different concern, but related sidebar UX)
+
+## Environment
+
+- Hermes Desktop v2026.7.7.2 (latest release)
+- Windows 10
+- Repro: create two sessions in different repos, switch between them in the sidebar → no way to jump to the corresponding workspace without manually `cd`ing in the embedded terminal.

### Problem or Use Case

## Summary

I would like to propose adding structured metadata to Hermes agent prompts that identifies the intended role or purpose of the prompt. This metadata would allow external gateways, routers, or inference layers to make intelligent model selection decisions before execution.

## Motivation

Many deployments use multiple LLMs with different strengths, costs, and latency characteristics. Today, routing decisions often rely on prompt inspection or heuristics, which can be brittle.

If Hermes exposed standardized prompt role metadata, infrastructure could reliably dispatch requests to the most appropriate model.

## Example Roles

Possible prompt categories could include:

* `orchestrator`
* `planner`
* `executor`
* `specialist:<domain>` (e.g. `specialist:code`, `specialist:sql`, `specialist:research`)
* `reviewer`
* `validator`
* `summarizer`
* `classifier`

The exact taxonomy is less important than providing a consistent, machine-readable indication of the prompt's intent.

## Example

```yaml
metadata:
  role: planner
```

or

```yaml
metadata:
  role: specialist
  specialty: coding
```

## Benefits

This would enable gateways to:

* Route planning tasks to reasoning-optimized models.
* Route coding tasks to code-specialized models.
* Send lightweight orchestration requests to smaller, faster models.
* Direct complex reasoning tasks to larger models.
* Optimize latency and infrastructure costs without relying on prompt parsing.
* Implement routing policies that are deterministic and easy to maintain.

## Use Case

Consider a deployment with an inference gateway in front of multiple LLMs:

* `planner` → reasoning model
* `orchestrator` → low-cost, fast model
* `specialist:code` → coding model
* `reviewer` → high-accuracy model

Instead of inspecting prompt contents, the gateway simply reads the metadata and forwards the request to the appropriate backend.

This approach keeps routing logic explicit, robust, and independent of prompt wording, while allowing organizations to optimize cost, latency, and quality across heterogeneous model deployments.


### Proposed Solution

Add a structured agent_metadata JSON field to the request payload exposing the agent role and capabilities (e.g., orchestrator, planner, specialist with domain), enabling external gateways to route requests to different models based on agent type without relying on prompt inspection.

# [Bug]: Desktop model picker reverts after selection — model switch does not persist

## Bug Description

In Hermes Desktop, switching models via the composer dropdown (Model Pill) does not persist. The selected model briefly appears but then reverts to the previous model. This happens even after waiting for the gateway to process the change.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Open Hermes Desktop with an active session
2. Click the model pill (dropdown) in the composer area
3. Select a different model from the dropdown menu
4. Observe: the model name briefly changes, then reverts to the original model
5. Wait any amount of time — the model still reverts

## Expected Behavior

After selecting a model from the dropdown, the model should persist and stay selected.

## Actual Behavior

The model selection reverts to the previous model. The user cannot switch models via the dropdown.

## Root Cause Analysis

The issue is in `currentPickerSelection()` in `lib/model-status-label.ts`:

```typescript
export function currentPickerSelection(
  hasSession: boolean,
  store: { model: string; provider: string },
  options?: { model?: string; provider?: string }
): { model: string; provider: string } {
  return {
    model: String((hasSession && options?.model) || store.model || options?.model || ''),
    provider: String((hasSession && options?.provider) || store.provider || options?.provider || '')
  }
}
```

**When `hasSession` is true, the gateway's `options.model` ALWAYS takes priority over `store.model` (the user's selection).**

The race condition flow:
1. User selects new model → `selectModel()` sets `$currentModel` (store) and calls `config.set` on gateway
2. `modelOptions` query is invalidated and refetches from gateway
3. Gateway hasn't processed `config.set` yet → returns OLD model in options
4. `currentPickerSelection()` sees `hasSession && options?.model` (old model) → uses it
5. UI reverts to old model

But the user reports that even after waiting, the model still reverts. This suggests the `config.set` call might not be persisting the model change correctly, OR the `modelOptions` query is not reflecting the updated state.

## Suggested Fix

The `currentPickerSelection` function should NOT override the store model with the gateway model when the user has just made a selection. One approach:

```typescript
export function currentPickerSelection(
  hasSession: boolean,
  store: { model: string; provider: string },
  options?: { model?: string; provider?: string }
): { model: string; provider: string } {
  // When the user has a store selection, prefer it over the gateway options.
  // The gateway options may be stale (race condition after config.set).
  // Only fall back to gateway options when store is empty.
  return {
    model: String(store.model || (hasSession && options?.model) || options?.model || ''),
    provider: String(store.provider || (hasSession && options?.provider) || options?.provider || '')
  }
}
```

Or alternatively, add a timestamp-based guard: after `selectModel()` is called, ignore gateway model updates for a short window (e.g. 2 seconds) to let the `config.set` propagate.

## Environment

- Hermes Desktop (latest from main, commit 5d9a72b7c)
- Windows 10
- Model: mimo-v2.5-pro via xiaomi API
- Session: active session with gateway connection

## Additional Context

- Related fix: `5a3092b60 fix(desktop): scope in-session /model switch per-session, stop process-env leak (#41120)` — this fixed cross-session model leakage but did not fix the picker revert issue
- Related fix: `8191f621c fix(gateway): preserve multiplex profile in model picker` — this fixed profile preservation but the revert issue persists
- The user confirms that waiting does not help — the model always reverts, suggesting the `config.set` result is not being reflected in the `modelOptions` query cache

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

items.body: ## Bug Description A healthy non-streaming provider call can be aborted by Hermes' 30-second wait-status heartbeat when the effective stale timeout is non-finite. The concrete production path is Mixture of Agents (MoA): - outer provider: moa - virtual base URL: moa://local - model preset observed: openai-xai-wide - implicit non-stream stale timeout: float("inf") If the call is still running when the heartbeat fires, Hermes formats the deadline with int(_deadline). For an infinite deadline this raises: ~~~text OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer ~~~ The generic retry layer then mislabels the local polling/display exception as an API failure, retries the otherwise healthy request five times, and ultimately makes the agent unavailable: ~~~text API call failed after 5 retries. cannot convert float infinity to integer ~~~ This is a regression introduced by [569b912d7d0931c7256e9f5fb326609e9deda377](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/569b912d7d0931c7256e9f5fb326609e9deda377) and remains present on upstream main at [007cd151329c20f9d3854b6338375f3188abc184](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/007cd151329c20f9d3854b6338375f3188abc184), verified 2026-07-16. ## Severity and User Impact This is user-blocking for affected configurations: - Interactive TUI turns fail, so the user cannot talk to the agent. - Scheduled/cron agent turns fail with the same exception. - Successful provider work can be discarded solely because it took longer than the UI heartbeat interval. - The error is attributed to the API even though it originates locally in the status formatter. - Retrying can start another request while the daemon worker for the prior healthy request is still running, creating a risk of duplicate load, latency, and provider cost. - Short calls appear healthy, making the failure intermittent until context size or provider load pushes latency beyond approximately 30 seconds. At inspection time, the exact exception appeared **2,552 times** across current and rotated agent.log/errors.log files. This is a count of matching log lines, not unique requests. The failures affected both TUI and cron paths and continued into 2026-07-16. ## Steps to Reproduce ### Runtime reproduction 1. Use a checkout containing commit 569b912 or current main. 2. Leave all stale-timeout overrides implicit: - do not set HERMES_API_CALL_STALE_TIMEOUT - do not configure a finite provider/model stale_timeout_seconds 3. Select a MoA preset whose outer route is provider=moa, base_url=moa://local. The observed preset was openai-xai-wide. 4. Start a non-streaming call that remains active for more than 30 seconds. A large conversation reliably exposes it, but a test double that sleeps for 31 seconds is sufficient. 5. At the first 100 × 0.3-second polling heartbeat, observe OverflowError. 6. The conversation loop retries and eventually reports the five-retry terminal error. The same trigger applies more generally to local/private endpoints whenever their generic stale timeout is infinite and no finite watchdog masks it at the heartbeat. ### Minimal mechanism reproduction Run from the Hermes repository: ~~~python from agent.model_metadata import is_local_endpoint assert is_local_endpoint("moa://local") is True deadline = float("inf") int(deadline) # OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer ~~~ Observed output on the affected installation: ~~~text True OverflowError: cannot convert float infinity to integer ~~~ A complete regression test should keep the non-streaming worker alive through the heartbeat while _compute_non_stream_stale_timeout() returns infinity; the test must verify that the call continues and that rendering the wait notice does not throw. ## Expected Behavior - A status/heartbeat update must never abort a provider call. - A healthy request that takes longer than 30 seconds must be allowed to finish. - If a finite watchdog is enabled, the notice should report the earliest applicable finite recovery deadline. - If no finite watchdog is enabled, the notice should omit the reconnect deadline or explicitly say there is no limit. - The retry layer should receive only genuine provider/transport failures, not status-formatting exceptions. ## Actual Behavior At approximately 30 seconds, the polling loop evaluates: ~~~python f"or overloaded; auto-reconnect at {int(_deadline)}s)" ~~~ When _deadline == float("inf"), interpolation raises before agent._emit_wait_notice(...) is called. The request is treated as failed and the generic five-retry policy runs. ## Timing Evidence A representative interactive TUI turn: ~~~text 2026-07-15 18:28:42.277 conversation turn started 2026-07-15 18:28:42.842 MoA reference call selected 2026-07-15 18:28:44.573 MoA aggregator selected 2026-07-15 18:29:12.579 attempt 1/5: OverflowError 2026-07-15 18:29:44.834 attempt 2/5: OverflowError 2026-07-15 18:30:20.693 attempt 3/5: OverflowError 2026-07-15 18:31:00.180 attempt 4/5: OverflowError 2026-07-15 18:31:51.232 attempt 5/5: OverflowError 2026-07-15 18:31:51.234 API call failed after 5 retries ~~~ The first failure is 30.302 seconds after the turn began, matching the heartbeat's 100 × 0.3-second cadence. Terminal log entry: ~~~text API call failed after 5 retries. cannot convert float infinity to integer | provider=moa model=openai-xai-wide msgs=103 tokens=~297,536 ~~~ The first exact occurrence was recorded at 2026-07-15 11:02:04 UTC, shortly after the update that introduced the wait-notice change. A separate cron turn also ended with: ~~~text API call failed after 5 retries. cannot convert float infinity to integer | provider=moa model=openai-xai-wide msgs=68 tokens=~148,286 ~~~ ## Provider/API Validation This is not an authentication, network, xAI, or OpenAI failure. The same captured request was sent directly through the provider path while bypassing interruptible_api_call(): - 3 of 3 controlled direct calls succeeded. - One successful call took 54.9 seconds. - Two additional calls both succeeded with 122.6 seconds combined elapsed time. - No credential or payload change was required. The representative captured request was approximately 1,313,799 bytes, with a Hermes log estimate of approximately 297,536 tokens. Aggregate character composition, without publishing private content: - system messages: 64,079 characters - tool results: 1,049,746 characters - current user content: 317 characters - tool schemas: 74,810 characters This explains why the issue becomes deterministic in a mature session: the provider legitimately needs more than 30 seconds, so the newly added display heartbeat executes. ## Affected Component - CLI / TUI interactive chat - Agent Core: non-streaming API polling and retry loop - Cron/scheduled agent execution - MoA virtual endpoints - Potentially any local/private endpoint whose implicit stale timeout resolves to infinity Messaging platform: N/A for the primary reproduction. The shared agent-core path means gateway-backed turns may also be exposed. ## Debug Report hermes debug share --local was run with redaction. A public paste was intentionally not uploaded because the complete report contains unrelated historical session, platform, and endpoint metadata. Relevant sanitized output: ~~~text version: 0.18.2 [71a012d7] (2026-07-16) os: Linux 6.1.0-50-cloud-amd64 x86_64 distribution: Debian GNU/Linux 12 (bookworm) python: 3.11.2 openai_sdk: 2.24.0 profile: default model: openai-xai-wide provider: moa terminal: local display.streaming: True ~~~ The bug was also verified directly in current upstream source, independently of the locally carried commits. ## Root Cause Analysis The failure chain is deterministic: 1. [is_local_endpoint()](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/007cd151329c20f9d3854b6338375f3188abc184/agent/model_metadata.py#L604-L660) treats an unqualified hostname as local. Parsing moa://local yields host local, so the function returns True. 2. [_compute_non_stream_stale_timeout()](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/007cd151329c20f9d3854b6338375f3188abc184/run_agent.py#L1312-L1325) returns float("inf") when the timeout is implicit and the base URL is local. 3. For the outer MoA route, agent.api_mode != "codex_responses", so the Codex TTFB watchdog is not enabled and does not replace the infinite generic deadline with a finite value. 4. The [30-second polling heartbeat](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/007cd151329c20f9d3854b6338375f3188abc184/agent/chat_completion_helpers.py#L605-L624) assigns _deadline = _stale_timeout and formats int(_deadline) without checking finiteness. 5. Although _emit_wait_notice() is documented as fail-open, Python evaluates the f-string before entering that helper. Its exception handling therefore cannot catch this conversion error. 6. The exception escapes the polling loop and is caught by the generic conversation retry layer, which reports it as an API failure. The regression commit added the deadline formatting. Before [569b912](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/commit/569b912d7d0931c7256e9f5fb326609e9deda377), the heartbeat only refreshed activity using elapsed time and did not convert the stale deadline. ## Why It Can Look Intermittent Calls completing before the first heartbeat never evaluate int(_deadline) and succeed. Fresh/short sessions are therefore less likely to fail. Large contexts, slow local inference, MoA aggregation, or temporary provider load push calls past 30 seconds and expose the bug every time. ## Temporary Workarounds Until a fix is merged: 1. Configure a finite timeout, for example: ~~~shell HERMES_API_CALL_STALE_TIMEOUT=900 ~~~ Then restart the relevant CLI/gateway/cron process. Equivalent finite values can be set through providers.<id>.stale_timeout_seconds or providers.<id>.models.<model>.stale_timeout_seconds. 2. Start a new/shorter session so requests are likely to finish before 30 seconds. This is only a probabilistic workaround. 3. Locally guard non-finite values before formatting the wait notice. Updating alone does not currently help because upstream main still contains the unsafe conversion. ## Proposed Fix Use math.isfinite() before every float-to-int conversion in wait/status formatting. More importantly, construct the notice from the actual enabled watchdogs: - generic wall-clock stale timeout, if finite - TTFB timeout before the first SSE event, if enabled and finite - event-idle timeout after the first SSE event, if enabled and finite - any applicable finite hard ceiling Report the earliest applicable finite deadline on the same request-relative timeline. If none exists, omit the reconnect suffix instead of claiming an automatic reconnect. The guard should be applied before building the f-string so display-only code cannot escape into the retry path. This should not change timeout semantics; it should only make status rendering safe and accurate. ## Acceptance Criteria - [ ] A MoA call using moa://local with an implicit infinite stale timeout can run beyond 30 seconds and return successfully. - [ ] A local/private non-streaming endpoint with an infinite generic timeout does not crash at any heartbeat. - [ ] No wait/status path converts inf, -inf, or nan to int. - [ ] Before the first Codex SSE event, the notice reports the finite TTFB deadline when that watchdog is enabled. - [ ] After an SSE event, the notice reports the finite stream-idle recovery deadline when applicable. - [ ] If every applicable watchdog is disabled or non-finite, no automatic-reconnect deadline is claimed. - [ ] Unexpected display callback/formatting errors remain fail-open and cannot trigger provider retries. - [ ] Focused regression tests cover the MoA outer route and local Codex routes before and after the first SSE event. - [ ] Existing finite-timeout behavior and stale-request recovery remain unchanged. ## Related Pull Requests Three open PRs currently address this incident: - [#64924](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/64924) — minimal guard rendering an infinite deadline as “no limit” - [#65594](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/65594) — guards multiple infinity-to-int conversions for MoA/local paths - [#65606](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pull/65606) — computes the earliest applicable finite watchdog and adds focused regression coverage All three were open and unmerged when this issue was prepared on 2026-07-16. This issue is intended to provide a canonical incident report, verified production evidence, and shared acceptance criteria—not to duplicate implementation work. ## Additional Privacy Note Raw prompts, session identifiers, credentials, user IDs, chat IDs, network addresses, and unrelated logs have been omitted. The timings and aggregate request measurements above preserve the relevant evidence without exposing conversation content. Additional targeted, redacted diagnostics can be provided if maintainers need them. ## Are you willing to submit a PR for this? There are already three active fix PRs, so I am not opening a fourth competing implementation. I can test a selected fix against the affected production path if useful.

## Bug Description

In the Hermes desktop app, when multiple chat sessions are open, user input in one session is occasionally routed to a different existing session for execution.

## Reproduction

1. Open multiple chat sessions in Hermes desktop
2. Type a message in session A
3. Occasionally, the message appears and gets executed in session B instead

## Environment

- Hermes desktop app (macOS)
- Multiple active sessions open

## Frequency

Intermittent — not consistently reproducible, but occurs often enough to be disruptive.

## Expected Behavior

User input in session A should always be processed in session A.

## Actual Behavior

User input in session A is sometimes processed in session B (a different existing session).

## Notes

- This is a UI/input routing issue, not a context overflow or delegation mechanism
- All sessions involved are pre-existing (not newly created)
- Related: #65659 (model switching bug in desktop UI)

items.body:
### Problem

All command descriptions in `COMMAND_REGISTRY` (`hermes_cli/commands.py`) are hardcoded in English. The Telegram adapter registers them verbatim via `set_my_commands()`, so non-English users see English descriptions in the `/` menu. This limits discoverability for users whose primary language is not English.

Directly editing `commands.py` works temporarily but is overwritten on every `hermes update`.

### Current code path

1. `hermes_cli/commands.py`: `telegram_bot_commands()` → `telegram_menu_commands()` produces `list[tuple[str, str]]` of `(name, description)` pairs
2. `plugins/platforms/telegram/adapter.py`: imports `telegram_menu_commands`, passes descriptions straight into `BotCommand(name, desc)` → `set_my_commands()`
3. No plugin hook, config override, or locale switch exists between the registry and the API call

### Proposed solution(s)

Any of the following would unblock localization without touching the core registry:

**Option A** — Config-based overrides in `config.yaml`:
```yaml
platforms:
  telegram:
    extra:
      command_menu:
        description_overrides:
          new: "Start a fresh session (new session ID + history)"
          help: "Show available commands"
```

**Option B** — A plugin hook (e.g. `on_command_menu`) that lets plugins rewrite descriptions before the Telegram adapter registers them.

**Option C** — A global `locale: zh_CN` / `locale: ja_JP` setting with a built-in translation table.

**Option D** — Add a `description_translations` field to `CommandDef` and a `locale` config knob; `telegram_bot_commands()` returns the localized description when available.

### Why this matters

- Telegram is one of Hermes' primary messaging platforms, with a large global user base
- Other platforms (Discord native slash commands, Slack) have the same problem
- A clean i18n mechanism prevents users from maintaining fork-level patches

items.title: [Bug]: Desktop Copy Image disappears for remote images above Chromium data URL IPC limit
items.body:
## Bug description

In Hermes Desktop connected to a remote backend, the **Copy Image** context-menu item disappears for larger images even though the image has loaded and is visibly rendered in chat.

A smaller image delivered through the same `MEDIA:` mechanism shows **Copy Image** correctly.

## Reproduction

1. Connect Hermes Desktop to a remote Hermes backend.
2. Deliver a PNG in assistant text using `MEDIA:/absolute/path/to/small.png`.
3. Right-click the rendered image. **Copy Image** is present.
4. Deliver a larger PNG through the same `MEDIA:` mechanism.
5. Right-click the rendered image. **Copy Image** is absent.

Concrete observed comparison:

| Image | PNG size | Estimated Base64 `data:` URL length | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Small, 2172×724 RGB PNG | 1,335,792 bytes | 1,781,078 characters | **Copy Image** present |
| Large, 1672×941 RGB PNG | 2,848,732 bytes | 3,798,334 characters | **Copy Image** absent |

Both files are normal, non-interlaced, 8-bit RGB PNGs with no alpha, ICC profile, or unusual PNG chunks. The assistant messages use the same `MEDIA:` syntax.

## Expected behavior

**Copy Image** should be available for every successfully loaded image, regardless of encoded file size.

## Actual behavior

For a remote image whose Base64 `data:` URL exceeds Chromium's roughly 2 MB cross-process URL limit, the image remains visible but the image-specific context-menu entries disappear.

## Root cause analysis

Remote gateway media is resolved through `gatewayMediaDataUrl()` / `readDesktopFileDataUrl()`, so the renderer displays the image with a Base64 `data:` URL.

The current Desktop context-menu code requires both an image media type and a non-empty `srcURL`:

```ts
const hasImage = params.mediaType === 'image' && Boolean(params.srcURL)
```

Current source:

https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/d0dcb9a5fd77aa8a6d7581372e64be0f2b1de409/apps/desktop/electron/main.ts#L4819-L4843

Chromium documents/practically enforces an approximately 2 MB URL IPC limit. Large `data:` URLs can be lost when passed from the renderer process to the browser process. This leaves `params.srcURL` empty, so Hermes sets `hasImage` to false and omits the complete image menu.

Chromium discussion:

https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-dev/c/zYYSVvn6a5M

The observed values align exactly with this boundary: 1.78 million characters works, while 3.80 million characters does not.

## Suggested fix

Do not use `srcURL` to decide whether the target is an image:

```ts
const hasImage = params.mediaType === 'image'
```

Use Electron's coordinate-based image copy operation for **Copy Image**:

```ts
window.webContents.copyImageAt(params.x, params.y)
```

Keep URL-dependent actions such as **Open Image**, **Copy Image Address**, and **Save Image As...** separately gated on a non-empty `params.srcURL`.

A regression test should cover:

```ts
{
  mediaType: 'image',
  srcURL: '',
  x: 100,
  y: 100
}
```

The expected menu should still include **Copy Image**, while URL-dependent actions may be hidden or disabled.

## Environment

- Hermes Agent/backend: v0.18.2
- Hermes Desktop: remote-backend mode
- Backend OS: Linux
- Current `main` checked on 2026-07-16 and still contains the affected logic

items.title: [Bug]: Cron scheduler installs profile secret scope unconditionally — breaks env-injected credentials on single-profile (non-multiplex) deployments → provider HTTP 401

labels.name: comp/agent
labels.description: Core agent runtime: loop, agent_init, prompt builder, context-compression, responses endpoint

labels.name: P1
labels.description: High — major feature broken, no workaround

labels.name: sweeper:risk-compatibility
labels.description: Sweeper risk: may break existing users, config, migrations, defaults, or upgrades

items.body:
## Summary

`cron/scheduler.py` wraps `run_job` in
`set_secret_scope(build_profile_secret_scope(<home>))` **unconditionally**. Every
interactive path in `gateway/run.py` installs that scope **only when
`multiplex_profiles` is on** (guarded by `if not multiplex_profiles: return
_run_agent_inner(...)`). The cron path is missing that guard.

On a **single-profile deployment where credentials are injected via the process
environment** (container env vars / systemd `Environment=` / a `.env` sourced into
the process, i.e. NOT written into `<home>/.env`), this asymmetry means:

- **Interactive** turns (multiplex OFF) skip the scope → `get_secret()` falls
  through to `os.environ` → provider key resolves → works.
- **Cron** jobs install a scope built only from `<home>/.env`. Since
  `build_profile_secret_scope()` returns *only* the parsed `.env` (it intentionally
  does not merge `os.environ`), and provider creds are non-global secrets, the
  scoped `get_secret("DEEPINFRA_API_KEY")` returns the default (empty). The
  resolver then ships `Authorization: Bearer no-key-required` and the provider
  responds **HTTP 401**.

This is a regression from the fix for #60726 (which correctly added the cron scope
wrapper for the multiplex-ON case, but without the `if not multiplex_profiles`
guard the interactive paths carry).

## Error

```
ERROR cron.scheduler: Job '<name>' failed: RuntimeError: HTTP 401: User is not authorized to access this resource
  File "/opt/hermes/cron/scheduler.py", line 3240, in run_job
    raise RuntimeError(_err_text)
```

Request dump shows the outgoing call carried the placeholder key:

```json
{
  "reason": "non_retryable_client_error",
  "request": {
    "url": "https://api.deepinfra.com/v1/openai/chat/completions",
    "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer no-key-required" },
    "body": { "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash", ... }
  }
}
```

## Root cause

`cron/scheduler.py` (~L3440):

```python
_scope_token = set_secret_scope(
    build_profile_secret_scope(_get_hermes_home())   # reads ONLY <home>/.env
)
```

vs. every interactive path, e.g. `gateway/run.py::_run_agent` (~L16984):

```python
if not getattr(getattr(self, "config", None), "multiplex_profiles", False):
    return await self._run_agent_inner(...)          # NO scope → os.environ
profile_home = self._resolve_profile_home_for_source(source)
with _profile_runtime_scope(profile_home):
    return await self._run_agent_inner(...)
```

The same guard exists at run.py L8518, L10736, L12348. The cron path has none.

## Reproduction

1. Single-profile deployment, `multiplex_profiles: false` (default).
2. Provide the inference provider key via the **process environment** only
   (`DEEPINFRA_API_KEY=...` as a container env var), NOT in `<home>/.env`.
3. Interactive chat on that provider works.
4. Create any cron job that makes an inference call.
5. On tick: `RuntimeError: HTTP 401` — the call went out with
   `Bearer no-key-required`.

Confirming probe (in the running process):

```python
from agent.secret_scope import get_secret, set_secret_scope, build_profile_secret_scope, is_multiplex_active
is_multiplex_active()                       # False
len(get_secret("DEEPINFRA_API_KEY"))        # 32  (no scope → os.environ)
set_secret_scope(build_profile_secret_scope("/home/.../data"))
len(get_secret("DEEPINFRA_API_KEY"))        # 0   (.env scope → missing)
```

## Suggested fix

Make the cron path mirror the interactive guard — do not install a profile scope
when multiplexing is off:

```python
from agent.secret_scope import is_multiplex_active
_scope_token = None
if is_multiplex_active():
    _scope_token = set_secret_scope(build_profile_secret_scope(_get_hermes_home()))
try:
    ...
finally:
    if _scope_token is not None:
        reset_secret_scope(_scope_token)
```

Alternatively (or additionally), have `build_profile_secret_scope()` overlay
`os.environ` under the `.env` (env-injected creds as a base, `.env` taking
precedence) so env-provided provider credentials remain visible to cron even when
a scope is installed. The guard is the minimal fix and matches the interactive
paths exactly.

## Environment

- Deployment: single-profile, `multiplex_profiles: false`
- Credentials injected as container env vars (Kubernetes `secretKeyRef`)
- Provider: `custom:deepinfra` (`deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash`)
- Symptom surfaces on the inference call; by the same mechanism any non-global
  secret a cron job reads *during* `run_job` (Tavily/web_search, Hindsight/memory)
  is also invisible under the cron scope. Delivery is unaffected (it runs after
  `reset_secret_scope`, back on `os.environ`).

## Related

- #60726 (closed) — origin; added the unconditional cron scope wrapper.
- #57736 (open) — `HERMES_CRON_SESSION` set process-globally; same class of
  cron/global-state coupling.
- #51603 (open) — `resolve_anthropic_token()` bypasses profile secret scope.
